Findings

  • The filter removes 98% of the raw gambling population. 10 685 of 10 863 gambling records carry no indicator tying them to Chile; the largest single block, 4 005 records, carries no captured reasoning text at all, and the next largest, 2 512 records, carries Vietnamese diacritics. Ranking operators by raw detection volume would direct effort almost entirely at operators serving other markets.
  • 125 of the 178 reported URLs map to VAT_NOT_PAID — 70% — meaning they match neither the registered-platform list nor the listed-brand list. 38 map to VAT_PAID and 15 to VAT_NOT_PAID_LISTED.
  • Replication is concentrated, not diffuse. The 178 reported URLs resolve to 124 root brands, and 71 of them are variants or redirects of an earlier domain rather than independently discovered sites. The largest cluster, doradobet.com, accounts for 9 reported URLs.
  • 28 reported domains carry a registered brand string without matching the registered domain. Examples include latamwinonline.com, betanochile1.com, betanochile.com. Under the mapping rules these fall to VAT_NOT_PAID, which is correct — but they are the population most likely to be trading on a registered brand, not the population least in need of attention.
  • Only 85 of the 178 reported URLs name Chile directly. A further 48 carry Spanish-language content with no market named, and 45 point at a specific neighbouring market while remaining reachable from Chile.

Most consequential implication

The reported set is small because the evidence supporting market relevance is thin, not because the activity is. 6 166 gambling records — 57% of the monitored population — were excluded for want of any market indicator, and 4 005 of those carry no captured reasoning text whatsoever. Enlarging the reported set is a capture problem before it is an analysis problem: until content is captured for those records, no market-relevance test of any design can adjudicate them, and the true size of the Chile-facing population remains unknown rather than small.

2. Scope and mapping rules

How 14 181 exported rows became 178 reported URLs, and what each VAT category does and does not assert.

StepRecordsRemovedGrounds
Export as supplied14 181—Semicolon-delimited detection export

Market-relevant17810 685Failed the market-relevance test (Annex B)

2.2 The three VAT categories

VAT_PAID
38

The domain, or an ancestor in its replication chain, matches a platform on the registered-platform list supplied with the report specification. Descendants inherit.

VAT_NOT_PAID_LISTED
15

The domain, or an ancestor, matches a brand recorded on the unregistered-brand list. Descendants inherit.

VAT_NOT_PAID
125

Gambling content matching neither list. This is a residual category, not a determination.

Two caveats that govern every VAT figure in this report

  1. Inheritance is an assumption, not a finding. VAT_PAID means the domain descends from a registered platform in the replication data — not that the domain itself sits inside that registration. A typosquat trading on a registered brand while operating outside its declared estate is indistinguishable from a genuine estate domain in this dataset. This is the group most in need of verification, not the group least in need of it.
  2. VAT_NOT_PAID means unlisted, not confirmed unregistered. An operator may hold a registration that is absent from the reference lists supplied. No record in this report should be read as a finding that a party has failed to register or to account for VAT.

2.3 How market relevance was determined

A record enters the reported set only if it carries gambling content and satisfies at least one relevance test. The tests are applied to the domain, the URL and the captured reasoning text for each record.

TestRule appliedReported URLs
A — direct market referenceThe string chile appears anywhere in the domain or URL including mid-string; or the domain ends in .cl; or carries a cl market marker as a label; or the captured content cites Chile, Chilean pesos or Santiago.85
B — Spanish content, uncontestedThe captured reasoning quotes Spanish site text and no competing non-Spanish market indicator is present.93
C — exclusion by competing localeNon-Latin scripts by Unicode range, locale-specific vocabulary, and currency or country markers exclude a record outright unless Test A is independently satisfied.— (excludes 10 685)

Spanish against Portuguese

The two languages are the hard case, and the discrimination is made on vocabulary that differs between them — apuestas against apostas, cuenta against conta, jugar against jogar, dinero against dinheiro, ruleta against roleta, tragamonedas against caça-níqueis, bienvenida against boas-vindas, giros gratis against rodadas grátis. Cognates that survive unchanged across the two languages are never treated as a Spanish signal: depósito in particular is spelled identically in Portuguese and would produce false positives at scale. 522 records were excluded on Portuguese vocabulary or a Brazilian real marker.

Terminology note

The source export labels its status field Illegal gambling. That label is relabelled to Gambling throughout this report. No record has been reclassified — the counts in this report reconcile exactly with the source file, and a reader auditing Annex A against the raw export will find the same rows under a different label.

The only content distinction this report draws is gambling against non-gambling. The report makes no assessment of whether any site or operator is licensed, unlicensed, lawful or unlawful, and no such determination should be inferred from a site's inclusion in it, from its appearance in any table or chart, or from the VAT category assigned to it. Where the report refers to a blocked-site list or to a registered-platform list, it is describing a list supplied to the analysis, not making a claim of its own.

4. Technique: a worked replication cluster

One cluster, resolved to its root and diffed character by character, shows the replication pattern that the aggregate figures summarise.

The Source field of the export encodes lineage as Variant (parent.domain) or Redirect (parent.domain). Parsing it yields a parent map; resolving each domain recursively to its root — with a cycle guard — attributes every domain to the brand that originated it rather than to its immediate parent. A seventh-generation replica is attributed to the originating brand, not to the sixth-generation domain that spawned it. No cycles were found in this export.

The cluster below is rooted at doradobet.com. Characters differing from the parent domain are marked.

Every domain in the cluster inherits VAT_PAID from its root under the mapping rules. Read against caveat 1, that inheritance is the assumption most worth testing: each of these domains resembles the registered brand closely enough to trade on it, and the data cannot distinguish an estate domain from a domain merely imitating one.

Which market each reported record actually addresses, where it is hosted in the namespace, and when it was detected.

45 reported URLs point at a specific neighbouring market rather than at Chile: Mexico (17), Peru (10), Argentina (10), Colombia (8). 5.5 Domains that are not straightforwardly operator estate

Two signals mark a domain that should not be treated as operator-owned property without a look first. An institutional suffix carrying gambling content indicates compromise or paid placement rather than an operator domain, and is a finding in its own right. A registrable domain that also appears in the non-gambling population is weaker: it may be a general-purpose site carrying a gambling page — affiliate carriage, a media comparison article — or simply an operator's own marketing and support pages classified separately. The signal says the domain is mixed, not that it has been compromised; which of the two it is has to be established by looking, and this report does not assert it.

6. Limits and data quality

What this report does not establish, what the inputs could not support, and what an auditor should check first.

6.1 The residual

The VAT mapping is scoped to two supplied reference lists. 10 649 gambling records — 98% of the monitored gambling population — match neither list and are therefore unassessed against any registration, not assessed and found wanting. Within the reported set alone the figure is 125 of 178. Any statement about the scale of unregistered activity would require a registration source this analysis does not have.

6.2 Observations on the reference lists

  • Corporate entries with no consumer brand named. skillonnet.com, baytreeinteractive.com, 418services.com appear on the registered-platform list as corporate domains without an accompanying consumer brand. The consumer brands they operate cannot be derived from the list, and any such brand appearing in the detection data will currently default to VAT_NOT_PAID. This gap is not quantifiable from the inputs supplied.
  • Mixed granularity. cl.bet7k.com, cl.novibet.com are listed with an operational subdomain rather than as bare domains, while every other entry is a bare domain. Matching normalises operational subdomains away, but the inconsistency suggests the list was assembled from more than one source.
  • A duplicate entry. latamwin.online appears twice on the registered-platform list. It is a single platform and is counted once.
  • Brand-level rather than domain-level entries. Entries such as betsson1001.com name one domain of a brand estate. A domain such as betsson.bet.ar does not match it and maps to VAT_NOT_PAID. Whether that is the intended reading is a question for whoever maintains the list; this report applies the rule as written.
  • Listed platforms absent from the export. baytreeinteractive.com, betsson1001.com, bettingiscool.com, kaizengaming.com, latamwin.online, skillonnet.com, winchile.com do not appear in this detection window at all, neither as a detected record nor as the parent of one.
  • Listed platforms present only as chain parents. 1xbet.com, cl.bet7k.com, epicbet.com, fortunazo.cl, state77.com appear only as the parent named in a replication chain, never as a detected record in their own right. Their descendants inherit VAT_PAID from a domain that was not itself observed in this window.

6.3 Data quality in the export

  • Blank reasoning text. 4 007 gambling records carry no captured reasoning at all — 37% of the gambling population. 4 005 of them are in the excluded set, where the absence of captured text is itself the reason for exclusion. These records are not dropped quietly: they appear in Annex B under the grounds no captured reasoning text.
  • Duplicate URLs. 6 rows repeat a URL already present. The first occurrence is retained; the duplicates are listed at the end of Annex B.
  • URL-encoding artefacts. 516 rows carry percent-encoded characters in the URL. These can produce apparent duplicates that differ only in encoding; de-duplication here is on the literal URL string and will not have collapsed them.
  • Deep operational subdomain stacks. A substantial number of domains in the export carry long repeated subdomain chains of the form mobile.support.account.mobile…. These are normalised away before brand extraction, but they inflate any count of distinct domains taken from the raw file.
  • Chain cycles. None. Every domain in the export resolves to a root without revisiting a domain already in its chain.
  • Non-gambling records under gambling roots. 3 312 records are classified non-gambling. Where such a domain shares a registrable domain with a reported gambling URL it is surfaced in section 5.5 rather than merged into the operator estate.

6.4 Reference-list provenance

No VAT reference file was attached to this report request. The registered-platform and listed-brand lists applied here were taken from the client's own report specification for the same saved search and the same market, held in the job repository. They were not re-derived, and nothing has been added to them. Before this report's VAT figures are relied on externally, those lists should be reconciled against a current reference file — if the lists have moved since that specification was written, every VAT figure in sections 1, 3 and 6 moves with them. The market-relevance analysis in sections 2, 4 and 5 does not depend on them.

6.5 Scope of the deliverable

The report specification also describes two CSV extracts — a report set matching Annex A, and a full mapped set covering every gambling URL with a market-relevance flag. This request named a single expected deliverable, report.html, so the CSVs were not produced. Annex A carries the full reported set including every column the report-set CSV would carry; the full mapped set would need a further run.

6.6 What an auditor should check first

  1. The 38 VAT_PAID records in Annex A, against the registered estates they are assumed to belong to. Inheritance is the least verified assumption in this report.
  2. The 28 brand-adjacent domains in section 3.2, which resemble registered brands without matching them.
  3. A sample of the 2 161 records excluded for no market indicator, against their captured reasoning text. Language misclassification is the most likely failure mode of the relevance test, and this is the bucket where it would hide.
